body: Social Security Act 2018 section 70 states that the purpose of the winter energy payment is to provide targeted financial assistance to help certain people meet household heating costs during the winter period.

Social Security Act 2018 section 71 defines qualifying benefit for Winter Energy Payment as a main benefit under the Act, New Zealand superannuation, or veteran's pension. It defines winter period for a calendar year as the 22-week period starting on 1 May, and defines relevant payment date for weekly or fortnightly instalments of the qualifying benefit.

Social Security Act 2018 section 72 entitles a person to Winter Energy Payment for days in the winter period if the person receives a qualifying benefit or portion of it, the qualifying benefit or portion is payable, and the person is not disqualified. Disqualifications include a partnered-rate case where MSD determines the spouse or partner is the 1 person entitled, a long-term hospital patient case terminated after review, residential care contribution cases for people aged 65 years or over or aged 50 to 64 years, specified disability residential care funding with redirected contributions, and an election not to receive the payment.

Social Security Act 2018 section 73 lets a person entitled to Winter Energy Payment elect not to receive it. For a relationship-rate payment, MSD must be satisfied the election is made by both spouses or partners. Unless revoked, the election stops entitlement for any days after the election is made.

Social Security Act 2018 section 74 pays Winter Energy Payment in 22 weekly instalments for recipients of a main benefit and in 11 fortnightly instalments for recipients of New Zealand superannuation or veteran's pension. The instalment is found by dividing the appropriate Schedule 4 Part 8 rate per winter period by 22 or 11, rounded up to the nearest whole cent, which is $0.01 and uses 100 cents per dollar, and then reduced for days in the week or fortnight for which the person is not entitled or the payment is not payable.

Social Security Act 2018 section 75 allows MSD to terminate a Winter Energy Payment after review if the beneficiary's qualifying benefit rate is required by section 206 to be reduced to the long-term hospital patient rate and continuing the payment is not consistent with the section 70 purpose.

Social Security Act 2018 section 220 provides that Winter Energy Payment is not payable while a beneficiary is absent from New Zealand unless it is payable under subsection (2). It is payable for up to a maximum of 28 days of any 1 or more absences during the winter period if the payment would be payable but for those days of absence and MSD is satisfied those absence days do not affect eligibility under section 72.

Social Security Act 2018 Schedule 4 Part 8 sets Winter Energy Payment rates per winter period at $450 for a person who is single and has no dependent children, $700 for a person who is single and has 1 or more dependent children, and $700 for a person who is in a relationship and is the 1 spouse or partner entitled under section 72(3). Clause 2 defines dependent child for this Part.
